facts.fact_text: On 6 May 2012 a public demonstration entitled the 'March of Millions' was held in central Moscow.
The 'March of Millions' demonstration on 6 May 2012 was held to protest against the allegedly rigged presidential elections.
The 'March of Millions' demonstration on 6 May 2012 had been approved by the Moscow city authorities in the form of a march followed by a meeting at Bolotnaya Square.
According to the applicant, on 6 May 2012 he arrived at Kaluzhskaya Square to take part in the 'March of Millions' demonstration.
According to the applicant, on 6 May 2012 he walked with other participants from Kaluzhskaya Square to Bolotnaya Square.
The applicant was arrested by the police on 6 May 2012 and taken to a police station before being released shortly after.
On 26 July 2012 the applicant was arrested on suspicion of having participated in acts of mass disorder on 6 May 2012.
On 27 July 2012 the Basmannyy District Court ordered that the applicant be placed in pre-trial detention until 26 September 2012.
On 1 August 2012 charges were brought against the applicant under Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation (participation in acts of mass disorder accompanied by violence).
On 21 February 2014 the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found the applicant guilty as charged.
The applicant was sentenced to three years and six months' imprisonment.

On 6 May 2012 the Moscow city department of the Investigative Committee of the Russian Federation opened criminal proceedings to investigate suspected acts of mass disorder under Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.

On 6 May 2012 the Moscow city department of the Investigative Committee of the Russian Federation opened criminal proceedings to investigate suspected violence against the police under Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.
On 1 August 2012 charges were brought against the applicant under Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation (participation in acts of mass disorder accompanied by violence).

Article 212 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation provides that the organisation of mass disorder, accompanied by violence, riot, arson, destruction of property, the use of firearms, explosives and explosive devices, as well as armed resistance to a public official, shall be punishable by four to ten years' deprivation of liberty.

Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation provides that participation in the types of mass disorder provided for by Article 212 § 1 shall be punishable by three to eight years' deprivation of liberty.

Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation provides that the use of violence which does not endanger life or health, or the threat to use such violence against a public official or his relatives in connection with the performance of his or her duties, shall be punishable by a fine of up to 200,000 roubles or an equivalent of the convicted person's wages for 18 months, or community service for up to five years, or up to five years' deprivation of liberty.
There were numerous clashes between the police and protestors at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012.

On 6 May 2012 the Moscow city department of the Investigative Committee of the Russian Federation opened criminal proceedings to investigate suspected acts of mass disorder under Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.

On 6 May 2012 the Moscow city department of the Investigative Committee of the Russian Federation opened criminal proceedings to investigate suspected violence against the police under Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that between 4 p.m. and 8 p.m. on 6 May 2012 at Bolotnaya Square, unidentified persons called those present to move outside the agreed meeting venue and to defy the lawful orders of the police.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that unidentified persons called those present at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012 to use violence, which led to mass disorder accompanied by the use of violence against public officials in connection with the performance of their duties and the destruction of property.
The march on 6 May 2012 was peaceful and held without any disruptions.
When the marchers arrived at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012, it became apparent that barriers installed by the police had narrowed the entrance to the meeting venue.
The barriers installed by the police at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012 allegedly restricted the space allocated for the meeting.
To control the crowd at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012, the police cordon forced the protestors to remain within the barriers.
According to the applicant, the police started to disperse the protesters at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012, using excessive force and beating them with truncheons.
According to the applicant, in response to the police dispersal, the protesters dragged metal barriers into place to protect themselves from the police.
According to the applicant, he grabbed the protester in the green T-shirt and pulled him back, trying to protect him from the truncheon blows.
The Basmannyy District Court's detention order of 27 July 2012 referred to the gravity of the charges against the applicant.

The Basmannyy District Court's detention order of 27 July 2012 referred to information about the applicant's character, including a report by Moscow Police's chief of department at the Centre for Counter-Extremism.
According to the report by Moscow Police's chief of department at the Centre for Counter-Extremism, the applicant was an active member of organisations of a destructive character.

According to the report by Moscow Police's chief of department at the Centre for Counter-Extremism, if the applicant were to stay at liberty, he planned to threaten witnesses, abscond and obstruct the investigation.
The Basmannyy District Court concluded on 27 July 2012 that the circumstances gave sufficient grounds to believe that the applicant was likely to flee to avoid the investigation and trial.

The Basmannyy District Court concluded on 27 July 2012 that the circumstances gave sufficient grounds to believe that the applicant was likely to destroy evidence or otherwise obstruct the investigation of the criminal case, which was still at an initial stage.
On 24 September 2012 the Basmannyy District Court granted the investigator's application and extended the applicant's pre-trial detention until 6 November 2012.
The Basmannyy District Court's extension order of 24 September 2012 was based on the finding that the circumstances justifying the original detention order had not changed.
On 29 October 2012 the Basmannyy District Court granted an extension of the applicant's pre-trial detention until 6 March 2013, essentially on the same grounds as earlier.
The Basmannyy District Court's extension order of 29 October 2012 noted that the circumstances justifying the detention order had not changed.
In the extension order of 29 October 2012 the Basmannyy District Court dismissed an objection from the applicant to the use of the operational-search reports concerning his character.
In the extension order of 29 October 2012 the Basmannyy District Court rejected the applicant's contesting of the alleged membership of any organisations of a destructive nature.
On 5 March 2013 the Basmannyy District Court granted a new extension of the applicant's pre-trial detention until 6 July 2013, essentially on the same grounds as before.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court's extension order of 6 June 2013 was based on the gravity of the charges and the finding that 'the reasons which initially warranted the detention have not changed'.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court's extension order of 6 June 2013 was based on the finding that 'no other measures of restraint would secure the aims and goals of the judicial proceedings'.

The applicant's request for an alternative preventive measure was dismissed by the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court on 6 June 2013 on the grounds that no other measure could secure the proper course of justice in the case.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court's extension order of 19 November 2013 was based on the gravity of the charges and the nature of the offences imputable to the defendants.
The applicant pleaded not guilty at trial and testified that he had decided to attend the public gathering on 6 May 2012.

The applicant testified that at the stage area he saw the mass beating of people by police officers and participants of the rally starting to bring forward metal barriers and to put them close to the police officers, trying to protect themselves from the latter.
The applicant testified that he was standing close to the barriers, taking his hands off when the police officers used their truncheons to hit over the barriers.
The applicant testified that he saw a group of five or six police officers who were trying to seize a young man in a green T-shirt and were hitting the man with their truncheons.

The applicant testified that, considering the young man in the green T-shirt was in danger because the police actions were unlawful, he tried to snatch him from the officers' hands by grasping the young man's waistband, pulling it and turning his back to protect him from the truncheon blows.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow considered the defendants' arguments that they were protecting somebody from police officers or happened to be victims of the police's use of force as farfetched and aimed at the mitigation of their responsibility.
